summary: Northwest Head light on Northwest Island in the Ramea Islands, off Newfoundland's southwest coast: lit in 1902 for local fishermen, still staffed, grounds open and tower closed.

light.fog_signal: horn, blast 3 s in every 30 s
light.note: Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24): LFl W 6s, flash 2 s and eclipse 4 s; horn blast 3 s, silence 27 s. Rowlett and the Town of Ramea: a white flash every 3 s. Lighthouse Friends gives the 1902 light as occulting white, with alternating periods of light and darkness of about 1.5 s. The record uses the Coast Guard entry.

structures.note: Coast Guard list: white cylindrical tower with red spiral band, 7.3 m. Rowlett: 9 m (30 ft) cylindrical cast-iron tower with lantern and gallery, painted red and white in a spiral; the measurement is undated. Lighthouse Friends: the 1902 tower was a cylindrical iron tower painted spirally in red and white. No source says whether the tower standing now is the 1902 tower.
White, flat-roofed dwelling joined to the tower by a covered way (Lighthouse Friends). Present state not given.

staffing.note: The Fisheries and Oceans brochure (page modified 2019-09-24) lists Northwest Head (Ramea) among the staffed lightstations. The Town of Ramea (undated) says resident keepers carry on the work.

access.note: Staffed lightstation: the keepers' home and workplace. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett, Town). Reached by car and passenger ferry from Burgeo, about one hour and twenty minutes; the boardwalk trail runs round the south of the island.

events.note: Station built in 1902 to serve local fishermen (Lighthouse Friends). Rowlett and the Town also give 1902.
Occulting white light described with the 1902 station; no lighting date within 1902 is given.
John Chaffey hired as first keeper; George Rossiter appointed assistant keeper by letter of 20 August 1902 at $150 a year (Lighthouse Friends).
Charles Chaffey succeeds his father. Heritage record: before 1920; the Town: around 1920; Lighthouse Friends' first date for him is 1921.
Air Marine Services installed a radio beacon near the light, in the 1950s (Lighthouse Friends).
Diaphone foghorn installed; a keeper and an assistant employed to tend the fog alarm, radio equipment and light (Lighthouse Friends).
Lighthouse converted to commercial electricity (Lighthouse Friends).

corrections.why: The station record gives a 1902 build date in its events but no first-lit year. Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett both date the station to 1902.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Coast Guard list (dated 2026-09-24): LFl W 6s. Rowlett and the Town: a white flash every 3 s. Lighthouse Friends: an occulting white light in 1902. The Coast Guard list is the most recent official entry and is the one recorded; the story gives the others.
Coast Guard list: 7.3 m. Rowlett: 9 m (30 ft), undated. The Coast Guard figure is recorded.
Heritage record: before 1920; the Town: about 1920; Lighthouse Friends: first date 1921. The story gives the spread as approximate.
Lighthouse Friends' keeper line spells the first keeper's name Cheffey; its text and the Town spell it Chaffey. The roster uses Chaffey.

notes_for_editor: Almost all of the 1902 history, the keeper line and the early keepers come from Lighthouse Friends. Its references are the Canadian Coast Guard's Newfoundland light list and the Town of Ramea site, so it is not an independent check. Heritage record: read through the HistoricPlaces.ca copy of the Heritage Foundation's property file (FPT 5088), not the file itself. Louis Kendall and Vincent Moores appear only in the Lighthouse Friends keeper line, with no role or dates beyond 'at least'; unverified elsewhere. Removed from the story in the fact-check (2026-10-28): the 1898 Life-Saving Service report's Table 67 (scan page 426; the OCR puts the printed page at 421 or 422, unconfirmed) lists 'Ramea Island' among places where American vessels stranded, and the 1895, 1896 and 1901 reports list it too. None of these entries gives a date, vessel or event, and no source ties any of them to the light, which was not built until 1902, so the story omits them. A human can decide whether 'Ramea Island' is the station's own island before any wreck is recorded here. The 1903 report's Table 67 also names Ramea Island (scan page 432); not used. Canadian Marine annual reports in the corpus (1900 to 1924) name none of the three stations as lights; the only Trepassey entry is a 1902 tide gauge. The Senate report 'Seeing the Light' (2010 staffing list) was not read for this station; the record's 'as of 2010' staffing rests on it. Chronicling America search for Ramea with 'lighthouse' returned no relevant page. Designer and builder of the 1902 station are not named in any source read. Wikipedia not used.
